stories.title: India issues flood alert as over 130 citizens missing in Nepal deluge
stories.summary: India has issued flood alerts in two northern states as floodwaters from Nepal approach the border, threatening downstream communities. At least 133 Indian tourists are missing after flash floods in Nepal, many pilgrims heading to Mount Kailash. India is conducting rescue operations and sending relief supplies, with Prime Minister Modi offering humanitarian aid to Nepal. India put parts of two of its northern states on high alert as floodwaters from neighbouring Nepal headed towards the border, while at least 133 citizens were among tourists missing after catastrophic flash floods swept through the Himalayan nation. The missing Indians were the largest group of foreign tourists affected, according to Nepalese tourism officials, with many of them pilgrims travelling toward Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus. India hasn’t put a number on the missing yet. The disaster is also threatening communities downstream in India. The country’s Central Water Commission warned a sudden rise in Nepal’s Trishuli river, about 160km from the Indian border, could travel downstream into the Gandak, a major river that crosses into India and runs through the densely populated state of Bihar before joining the Ganges. “State government of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have taken measures such as required evacuation and other support to local Indian communities near the India–Nepal border,” according to a statement. “Both states have been advised to remain alert and maintain close monitoring of the situation.” The two states together are home to more than 300 million people. “No panic-like situation has arisen,” it added.

The missing Indians were the largest group of foreign tourists affected, according to Nepalese tourism officials, with many of them pilgrims travelling toward Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus.
India hasn’t put a number on the missing yet.
The disaster is also threatening communities downstream in India.

stories.title: Nine dams in Malaysia at warning level, one at critical level
stories.summary: Sungai Pagar Dam in Labuan remains at critical water level, while nine other dams in Malaysia are at warning status, with Johor having the most affected reservoirs. Perlis prepares cloud-seeding to raise Timah Tasoh Dam levels after its status improved from critical to warning. MetMalaysia warns of prolonged dry spells and below-average rainfall until early next year, increasing drought risks in several Malaysian regions. Sungai Pagar Dam in Labuan remains at a critical water level, but Timah Tasoh Dam in Perlis has improved from critical to warning status in the latest dam-level monitoring by the National Water Services Commission (SPAN). The update, displayed at SPAN’s war room on Aug 26, showed that nine dams are now at warning level while two others are at alert level. Apart from Timah Tasoh, the dams on warning status are Lower Layang, Upper Layang, Lebam, Gunung Pulai 1, Gunung Pulai 2 and Pontian Kechil in Johor, as well as Muda and Ahning in Kedah. Labong dams in Johor and Jus dams in Melaka remain at alert levels. The latest reading narrows the number of dams at critical status to one, after Timah Tasoh was previously listed alongside Sungai Pagar as being at that level the previous day. However, the overall picture remains a concern, with 12 dams still classified as being at critical, warning or alert levels. Johor accounts for the largest number of affected reservoirs, with six dams at warning level – Lower Layang, Upper Layang, Lebam, Gunung Pulai 1, Gunung Pulai 2 and Pontian Kechil – and Labong at alert level. Sungai Pagar’s continued critical status will also require close monitoring, including the availability of alternative water sources and measures to ensure consumers in the areas it serves are not affected. The improved status at Timah Tasoh comes after the Perlis dam had been placed at a critical level.

stories.title: Humanoids have bodies. They still need brains.
stories.summary: China's humanoid boom has solved the most visible part of the problem: figuring out how to hobble together a body. The harder part now is building a brain.
